story.head: The Flames come in rested
paras: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Flames (7-8-1) lost 2-1 in overtime to Seattle on Wednesday, while the Ducks have won three straight. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Ducks fourth (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Flames fifth (tied for 24th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Ducks’ record (.531) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.473), largely thanks to their finishing. The Flames’ record (.469) is about what their chances are worth.

The Ducks are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd), give up a lot of dangerous shots (30th) and have had shaky goaltending (29th). Anaheim has allowed 3.81 goals a game, the third most in the league. As for the Flames, they take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (30th). Calgary has scored 2.44 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Ducks. Beyond that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Leo Carlsson (5 G / 19 A / 24 P in 16 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring and is seventh in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Calgary. Cutter Gauthier (11 G / 6 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for fifth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Matt Coronato (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 16 GP) is next in line.
Lukáš Dostál (4-4-1 / .872 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Anaheim, and Dustin Wolf (3-4-1 / .870 SV% in 8 GS) for Calgary.
At home, Ryan Huska likes to send Farabee, Backlund and Coronato out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Gauthier, Granlund and Sennecke.

The Flames are newly without Maxim Tsyplakov, have been without Samuel Honzek and Connor Zary for several games, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season.
